country: Multiple (including Germany and other countries; three largest national subgroups analyzed)
models_evaluated: machine learning-based personalized upper limit of normal model for 5R-STS test

links.outcome: Model prediction error of 5R-STS times on external healthy cohort versus observed
links.effect: RMSE 2.33 s, MAE 1.70 s, R2 0.064; mean bias -1.1 s; personalized ULN flagged OFI in 17.5% vs 6.4% with generalized threshold; systematic underestimation of slower times.
links.quote: In this external validation, the model demonstrated limited generalization including a systematic underestimation of slower test times and insufficient personalized ULN calibration.

links.outcome: Performance differences across test setting and country compared with single-center development data
links.effect: Remote testing associated with greater prediction bias (adjusted mean difference -0.90 s) and higher odds of ULN exceedance (adjusted OR 10.7); differences across three largest national subgroups.
links.quote: Multivariable regression analyses showed that remote testing was independently associated with greater prediction bias and higher odds of personalized ULN exceedance compared with supervised testing (adjusted mean difference: - 0.90 s; adjusted OR: 10.7).

links.outcome: External-cohort performance of model developed on single-center data
links.effect: Limited external generalization: R2 0.064, systematic underestimation of slower test times, insufficient personalized ULN calibration.
links.quote: These findings indicate that external validity of models derived from single-center data can be limited, underscoring the importance of comprehensive external validation and, potentially, multicenter retraining before clinical implementation.

screen.reason: The study conducts an external validation of an existing machine learning web application for personalized functional impairment thresholds (evaluating usability, remote vs supervised settings, and subgroup performance), but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
